meta.title: $100 in 1871: Stocks vs Gold vs Inflation (155 Years)
meta.description:
What happened to $100 invested in January 1871? In US stocks with dividends reinvested it grew to about $118.7 million. In gold it became $21,340. Meanwhile prices rose about 27-fold. This animation walks through the 1929 crash, the gold standard, Nixon's 1971 decision, the 1980 gold spike and the 2008 crisis.

Educational only. Not investment advice.
meta.sources: Shiller, gold price data, US BLS
meta.sources_long: Robert Shiller's S&P 500 data, extended with FRED prices after mid-2023 (github.com/datasets/s-and-p-500); gold prices from Timothy Green's historical table and the World Bank Pink Sheet (github.com/datasets/gold-prices); US CPI-U from the BLS (github.com/datasets/cpi-us). Dividends after mid-2023 estimated at a 1.3% yield.

scenes.title: What $100 From 1871 Became
scenes.subtitle: US stocks (S&P 500, dividends reinvested) vs gold vs consumer prices, log scale
scenes.source: Sources: Robert Shiller and FRED (S&P 500), Timothy Green and World Bank (gold), US BLS (CPI). Dividends after mid-2023 estimated at a 1.3% yield. Before taxes and fees.

captions.text: Put $100 into US stocks (dividends reinvested), $100 into gold, and watch what $100 of shopping costs over time.
Gold doesn't move. It can't: the US fixes its price at $20.67 an ounce.

captions.chapter: Crash, war and the gold standard
captions.text: Stocks lose 82% by 1932, even with dividends. Gold holds steady.
The US raises the official gold price from $20.67 to $35. Gold jumps 69% overnight.
Post-war boom. Stocks leave both gold and prices far behind.
Nixon ends the dollar's link to gold. Gold is finally free to find its own price.
Gold spikes to $675, then falls for almost 20 years.
Dot-com bust, then 2008: stocks fall 49% peak to trough. Gold rises 4.0x.
Over every 20-year stretch since 1871, stocks with dividends reinvested never lost money in dollar terms.
$100 became $119M in stocks, $21.3K in gold. Prices rose 27-fold.
